title: Tenant thundering herd: gentle quarantine + model-fallback for upstream 5xx bursts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A major customer reported a surge of 5xx errors and long tail timeouts across Hosted endpoints during a large ingestion job. Investigation shows a correlated spike of upstream model-backed errors from an external model provider combined with aggressive client SDK retries, which created a tenant-local thundering herd and caused our inference frontends to hit connection/backpressure limits. This ticket implements a short-lived per-tenant quarantine window with progressive cool-off and an automated fallback to a smaller, compatible model variant to preserve customer traffic while we remediate upstream failures.

Impact: Affected customer reported ~15% request errors and 2x token latency for ~27 minutes during the incident window. Multiple downstream requests were retried by clients, amplifying transient failures into an operational incident. High-priority for P0 customer SLA and to avoid repeated escalations.

Goals: 1) Stop retry amplification and avoid cross-tenant spill; 2) Keep best-effort traffic flowing using a safe fallback model pathway; 3) Provide clear telemetry and automated rollback; 4) Surface customer-facing mitigation notes for support teams.
steps_taken: 2026-03-01 09:12 — Oncall intake: support received multiple customer reports; opened initial incident channel and collected traces (trace IDs prefixed with trace-cc-*)
2026-03-01 09:25 — Temporary mitigation: edge admission soft-throttle deployed (10m) to reduce immediate retry fanout
2026-03-01 09:40 — Correlated with third-party model provider errors (5xx spike) via partner telemetry; flagged as upstream service degradation
2026-03-01 10:05 — Implemented manual tenant quarantine for affected customer (10m window) and informed support to alert customer; gathered logs for postmortem
2026-03-02 11:00 — Engineering triage: decided long-term automated quarantine + model-fallback approach preferable to global backoff rules
2026-03-03 14:20 — Design sketch and rollout plan created in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RI/ENG-397205-fallback-quarantine (internal)
investigation_notes: Root cause: transient upstream model container failure at the provider caused disproportionate 5xx responses for a specific model family. Our frontends attempted retries with default SDK behavior, causing connection pile-up and k/v cache eviction under pressure.
Key signal: simultaneous increases in connection wait-queue length, request queue latency, and an uptick of 'upstream-502' tags in our edge logs between 09:10-09:40 UTC.

Reproduction: Synthetic replay of the customer workload against a staging proxy that injected 50% 5xx responses reproduced connection stalls and client-side retry amplification at ~2x baseline error rate.
decisions: Adopt per-tenant soft quarantine: when a tenant exceeds X 5xx responses within Y seconds, mark it as 'throttle-candidate' and apply a progressive cool-off rather than immediate hard-drop.

Fallback policy: if quarantine triggers AND a compatible lower-cost/smaller model exists (catalog tag 'compatible-fallback'), route a degraded best-effort path to that model variant with strict token/time limits.
Retries: override SDK auto-retries for quarantined tenants — only a single server-side hedged attempt to preferred backend and then fallback; return a clear retry-able header for clients to honor.
Telemetry: surface a tenant quarantine metric in Console (per-tenant quarantine_count, quarantine_duration, fallback_routing_rate).
Safety: quarantine logic must be idempotent, scoped to deployment unit, and include automatic expiry with optional manual override by SRE.
Rollout: staged in hosted region us-west-2, feature-flagged and gradually ramped (2% -> 25% -> 100%) with kill-switch.
Customer comms: support to send targeted update if quarantine affects production traffic.
implementation_notes: Runtime change: add tenantQuarantine controller in admission stage to evaluate short-window 5xx rates; expose REST toggle in control plane.
Router change: allow an ordered list of routing candidates (primary, fallback) returned by model-catalog; router will attempt primary once then fallback without multiple retries.
SDK guidance: update official python/js SDKs to recognize 'Quarantine-Notice' header and suppress client retries for 60s; ship patch PRs linked below.
Observability: add Grafana dashboard 'Quarantine Events by Tenant' and alert policy for >5 quarantines/min across accounts.
Safety tests: unit + integration harness simulating mixed 200/502 traffic; e2e staging run with synthetic customer load for 1 hour.
Backfill: migration to ensure existing routing configs include fallback model IDs for top 20 customers; otherwise fallback path returns explicit 503 with guidance.
comments: 2026-03-02 09:15 — Ruth Nguyen (SRE): Observed same behavior in dedicated clusters; recommend we include Dedicated routing controller hooks in the first rollout to avoid gap.
2026-03-04 16:40 — Mateo Li (assignee): Initial controller unit tests passing; integration tests flaking on connection-reset simulation. Investigating stub timing in test harness.
2026-03-06 10:02 — Aisha Patel (creator): Support prepared customer note template; waiting on SDK patch to suppress client retries before broad ramp.
2026-03-08 08:30 — QA (Emily Zhang): Staging run completed for 120m with synthetic 40% 5xx injection; quarantine triggers and fallback routing observed; no additional cross-tenant impact seen.

2026-03-09 13:50 — Pedro Alvarez (Eng): Deployed 2% canary in us-west-2 for 6 hours; quarantine heatmap shows expected suppression of retry amplification. No regressions in throughput after fallback activation.
next_steps: Finalize SDK patches and publish minor releases (js/py) with guidance for clients to honor Quarantine-Notice header.
Complete rollout staging -> 25% -> 100% with 1-hour observation windows between ramps.
Run post-deployment load test with partner model provider to validate behavior under realistic degraded upstream scenarios.
Draft postmortem and customer-facing summary (support+comms) after closure and include recommended SDK upgrade in advisory.
Add follow-on RFC to explore proactive cross-provider hedging when an upstream provider shows sustained error signals.
